body:
This PR updates the watchtower update schedules to provide better deployment cadence and cleans up domain references in documentation.

## Background

The current watchtower setup had production services updating weekly, which was too conservative, and canary services updating daily, which wasn't aggressive enough for early testing. Also found some domain-specific references in documentation that needed to be generalized.

## Changes

**Watchtower Schedule Updates:**
- Production services: Weekly → Daily (24 hours)  
- Canary services: Daily → Hourly (1 hour)

This gives us daily stable updates for production while canary aggressively tests the latest versions hourly.

**Documentation Cleanup:**
- Updated README.md to use generic domain examples
- Simplified domain structure documentation (removed machine ID suffixes)
- Cleaned up documentation references

## Testing

Verified both watchtower services restart correctly with new schedules:
- Production watchtower: Next check in ~24 hours
- Canary watchtower: Next check in ~1 hour

Container logs confirm the new timing is active.

body: This is an automated attempt to fix a deployment failure detected in history #925. The AI analyzed the deployment logs and proposed the following changes. Diagnosis: The Vercel deployment failed due to a 401 Unauthorized error during the health check. This indicates that the application requires authentication and the health check request isn't providing the necessary credentials. Since the application is a simple Next.js app and the recent changes only involved updating the README, and removing server-side code, the most likely reason is that some server-side authentication middleware was removed or misconfigured, inadvertently making the entire application require authentication.  The current `pages/index.js` file is being served as a protected resource, resulting in the 401 error.  The solution is to create a basic, unprotected Next.js app.

body:
## Problem

When users select "Ship to a different address?" on the checkout page, the T-Cat shipping API was incorrectly using the `shipping_phone` meta field for the `RecipientMobile` parameter instead of the required `shipping_mobile_01` field.

## Solution

Updated the recipient mobile phone logic in `class-tcat-order.php` to use the correct meta field name:

- **When "Ship to different address" is checked**: Now uses `shipping_mobile_01` instead of `shipping_phone`
- **When "Ship to different address" is NOT checked**: Continues to use `billing_phone` as before
- **Fallback behavior**: Maintains the existing fallback chain (meta field → standard WooCommerce field)

## Changes Made

```php
// Before
$shipping_phone = $order->get_meta( 'shipping_phone', true );

// After  
$shipping_phone = $order->get_meta( 'shipping_mobile_01', true );
```

## Testing

The fix has been validated for all scenarios:
- ✅ Different shipping address with `shipping_mobile_01` present
- ✅ Different shipping address without `shipping_mobile_01` (falls back to billing phone)  
- ✅ Same address (uses billing phone)
- ✅ Guest checkout (works with all scenarios)

This change ensures the T-Cat API receives the correct mobile phone number based on the user's shipping preference while maintaining backward compatibility and guest checkout support.

body: # Description This PR fixed the bugs in the fw_util.json configuration file for the Icecube platform. # Motivation Based on the previous PR https://github.com/facebook/fboss/pull/497 submission, we found two bugs in our Icecube's fw_util.json file. These bugs are related to the commands `gpioset gpiochip0 10=0` for pic_cpld1 and `gpioset gpiochip0 9=0` for pic_cpld2, and need to be fixed. To operate pic_cpld1, the following commands must be executed first: `gpioset gpiochip0 65=1` `gpioset gpiochip0 10=0` To operate pic_cpld2, the following commands must be executed first: `gpioset gpiochip0 66=1` `gpioset gpiochip0 9=0` 1. To reproduce this error for pic_cpld1: If we first execute the command `gpioset gpiochip0 10=1`, And then execute this command: `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=./fboss_lib/ ./bin/fw_util --config_file ./fw_util.json --fw_action=read --fw_target_name=pic_cpld1 --fw_binary_file=pic_cpld1.bin`, an error will occur. 2. To reproduce this error for pic_cpld2: If we first execute the command `gpioset gpiochip0 9=1`, And then execute this command: `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=./fboss_lib/ ./bin/fw_util --config_file ./fw_util.json --fw_action=read --fw_target_name=pic_cpld2 --fw_binary_file=pic_cpld2.bin`, an error will occur. **To fix this error**: 1. In the `preUpgrade` section, use the `gpioset` command type to directly set `gpioset gpiochip0 10=0` and `gpioset gpiochip0 9=0` instead of using the original `gpioget` operation. 2. Also fixed a `gpioChipPin` number error for dom_fpga2. # Test Plan The fixes have been verified on hardware. commit: 79653438f55dbf9e790e536759137c26e63d367f test logs: [icecube_fw_util_reproduce_the_bug_9_11.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22287909/icecube_fw_util_reproduce_the_bug_9_11.txt) [icecube_fw_util_fix_the_bug_9_11.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22287912/icecube_fw_util_fix_the_bug_9_11.txt) [icecube_fw_util_fix_dom_fpga2_bug_9_11.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22287940/icecube_fw_util_fix_dom_fpga2_bug_9_11.txt)

author: carljm
body:
## Summary

Use `Type::Divergent` to short-circuit diverging types in type expressions. This avoids panicking in a wide variety of cases of recursive type expressions.

Avoids many panics (but not yet all -- I'll be tracking down the rest) from https://github.com/astral-sh/ty/issues/256 by falling back to Divergent. For many of these recursive type aliases, we'd like to support them properly (i.e. really understand the recursive nature of the type, not just fall back to Divergent) but that will be future work.

This switches `Type::has_divergent_type` from using `any_over_type` to a custom set of visit methods, because `any_over_type` visits more than we need to visit, and exercises some lazy attributes of type, causing significantly more work. This change means this diff doesn't regress perf; it even reclaims some of the perf regression from https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/20333.

## Test Plan

Added mdtest for recursive type alias that panics on main.

Verified that we can now type-check `packaging` (and projects depending on it) without panic; this will allow moving a number of mypy-primer projects from `bad.txt` to `good.txt` in a subsequent PR.

To fix the problem, set an explicit `permissions` block restricting the job or workflow to the least privilege required. In this case, both jobs (`rust_check_format`, `rust_check_doc`) only check formatting or build documentation; they do not modify the repository or interact externally. The minimal needed privilege is `contents: read`.

Apply the fix at the root of the workflow (top-level), just after the workflow `name` and `on` triggers, to cover all jobs in this workflow. Add the following block:
```yaml
permissions:
  contents: read
```
This ensures that all jobs in the workflow only get read access to repository contents.
